page: Microsoft Azure D32als_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine within the Dalsv7 series, powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio indicative of a compute-focused or low-memory profile. The instance contains no bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread and vectorized integer capabilities. Stress-ng single-core performance ranks in the top tier, supported by top-quartile PassMark CPU encryption scores (35,423.04) and compression throughput reaching 34.83 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip. Multi-threaded decompression in bzip3 reaches 214.27 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. In AI workloads, CPU-based LLM token generation exhibits strong marks for smaller models, achieving 292.08 tokens/sec on 135M models and 30.51 tokens/sec on 7B models. Memory-intensive and full multi-core stress operations, such as the overall stress-ng multi-core metric and PassMark database operations, settle within the average range.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio delivers cost efficiency for processing tasks that prioritize raw CPU cycles over high RAM density, avoiding the overhead of unneeded memory allocation. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local ephemeral NVMe disks and GPUs, meaning all I/O depends on remote storage solutions. Microsoft Azure D32als_v7 is suited for compute-heavy batch processing, continuous integration pipelines, data compression pipelines, static web serving clusters, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
